overview.title: 📖 Overview: When Is Grain 'Bread'?
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 37a–37b
overview.hebrewSource: כֹּל שֶׁהוּא מֵחֲמֵשֶׁת הַמִּינִים מְבָרְכִין עָלָיו בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי מְזוֹנוֹת
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens by finishing the analysis of Rav and Shmuel's twin rulings about the five species of grain: one statement covers mixtures, the other excludes rice and millet. But a Tosefta says that rice which was ground, baked and cooked gets borei minei mezonot, and after several attempts to pin that Tosefta on Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, the Gemara declares Rav and Shmuel conclusively refuted. From there the daf turns to the blessing after eating: Rabban Gamliel requires the full Grace after Meals for the seven species, the Rabbis one abridged blessing, and Rabbi Akiva boldly follows the majority in Rabban Gamliel's presence. The last section asks when bread that has been broken, soaked or cooked still deserves hamotzi, and closes with odd flatbreads and their status for ḥalla.

slides.title: 🍚 Rice: A Refutation of Rav and Shmuel
slides.subtitle: Every proof that rice is 'not grain' meets a baraita that treats it like grain

nodes.content: 📜 Rav and Shmuel: 'anything that has of the five grains' teaches mixtures; 'anything that is of the five grains' excludes rice and millet, even pure
❓ But a baraita: rice bread or millet bread — bless before and after 'like a cooked dish', and a cooked dish gets mezonot before and me'ein shalosh after!
💡 'Like a cooked dish' in having blessings before and after; not like it in which blessings: here shehakol before and borei nefashot after
❓ But another baraita lists rice among the cooked dishes (ḥilka, teraggis, flour, zariz, arsan, and rice)!
💡 That is Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri, who says rice is grain: karet for its leaven, and matza from it fulfills the Passover obligation. The Rabbis disagree
❓ But the Tosefta: rice ground, baked and cooked gets mezonot — if that were Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri it would say hamotzi and three blessings. So it must be the Rabbis!
⛔ תְּיוּבְתָּא — a conclusive refutation of Rav and Shmuel

slides.title: 🌾 The Tosefta: Wheat and Rice From Kernel to Dish
slides.subtitle: What form the grain is in decides both the blessing before and the blessing after
rows: בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה (the Rabbis); Rabbi Yehuda: borei minei zera'im, 'various kinds of seeds'
Wheat ground, baked, then cooked — slices intact
Three blessings of Grace after Meals
One blessing abridged from three (me'ein shalosh)
Rice ground, baked, then cooked — even with pieces intact
Me'ein shalosh as taught — but the Gemara emends: 'nothing', i.e. only borei nefashot

callout.label: Why emend?
callout.text: Rav Sheshet first assigns 'me'ein shalosh after rice' to Rabban Gamliel. But the Tosefta's wheat clause (dissolved slices → me'ein shalosh) cannot be Rabban Gamliel, who requires three blessings even for dates. So the whole Tosefta is the Rabbis, and its rice ending is corrected to match their view that no blessing of the Land follows rice.

slides.title: 🍯 After Dates in Jericho: Rabban Gamliel vs. Rabbi Akiva
slides.subtitle: The dispute over the blessing after the seven species, and a student who follows the majority

lines.speaker: Baraita
lines.text: Anything from the seven species: Rabban Gamliel says three blessings of Grace after Meals; the Sages say one blessing abridged from three.

lines.speaker: Story
lines.text: Rabban Gamliel and the elders reclined in an upper room in Jericho, ate dates, and Rabban Gamliel gave Rabbi Akiva permission to bless. Rabbi Akiva hurried and recited me'ein shalosh.

lines.speaker: R' Gamliel
lines.text: Akiva! How long will you stick your head into the dispute?

lines.speaker: R' Akiva
lines.text: Our teacher, though you say this and your colleagues say that, you taught us: individual and many — the halakha follows the many.

lines.speaker: R' Yehuda
lines.text: A variant in Rabbi Akiva's name: seven species that are not grain, or grain not made into bread — Rabban Gamliel: three blessings; Sages: one. Neither seven species nor grain, such as rice or millet bread — Rabban Gamliel: me'ein shalosh; Sages: nothing.

lines.speaker: Rav Sheshet
lines.text: So a baraita saying 'nothing after rice' and a Tosefta saying 'me'ein shalosh after rice' need not conflict — one is the Rabbis, the other Rabban Gamliel.

callout.label: In the end:
callout.text: The Gemara prefers to keep the Tosefta entirely with the Rabbis and emend its rice clause, rather than split one Tosefta between two tannaim.

slides.title: 🍞 When Do Bread Crumbs Still Get Hamotzi?
slides.subtitle: Rav Yosef's olive-bulk rule is tested against the meal-offerings and finally replaced

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rav Yosef: a cooked dish (ḥavitza) with bread pieces of an olive-bulk — hamotzi and three blessings; smaller pieces — mezonot and me'ein shalosh
2️⃣ His proof: a priest eating meal-offerings in Jerusalem says hamotzi (after sheheḥeyanu the first time), and 'he crumbles them all into olive-bulk pieces'

3️⃣ Abaye: then for the school of Rabbi Yishmael, who crush the offering back to flour, no hamotzi? Yet a baraita says one who gathers an olive-bulk of those crumbs is liable to karet if leavened and fulfills matza if unleavened — crumbs are still bread!
4️⃣ Answer: the crumbs were kneaded back into one mass. Rejected: the baraita says 'ate them' within the time of eating a half-loaf, not 'ate it'
5️⃣ Better answer: the crumbs came from a large loaf that already had bread status
6️⃣ Conclusion — Rav Sheshet: even without olive-bulk pieces, hamotzi. Rava: provided it still has תּוֹרִיתָא דְנַהְמָא, the appearance of bread

callout.label: Ḥalla footnote:
callout.text: Terokanin (a watery batter roasted in a hole in the ground, per Abaye) are said to be obligated in ḥalla, but Ravin reports Rabbi Yoḥanan exempting them. Terita, variously a batter poured on a hot stove, Indian skewer-bread, or bread made for kutaḥ, is exempt. Rabbi Ḥiyya exempts kutaḥ-bread; Rabbi Yehuda says the shape tells: thick loaves obligated, board-shaped exempt.

slides.title: 🥣 Rava's Rihata: Farmers vs. Meḥoza
slides.subtitle: A flour-and-honey porridge, blessed by its primary ingredient — until Rava changes his mind

boxes.title: Meḥoza Rihata
items: They do not add extra flour
שֶׁהַכֹּל נִהְיֶה בִּדְבָרוֹ — Rava's first ruling

boxes.title: Rava's Retraction
items: Because Rav and Shmuel said anything containing the five species of grain gets mezonot
The grain's presence, not its proportion, decides

callout.label: Note:
callout.text: Rava relies on the very rule of Rav and Shmuel that the daf's opening refuted with regard to rice. The refutation concerned rice and millet; the principle that grain in a mixture governs the blessing stands.

summary.principle: The five species of grain govern the blessing wherever they are present, rice does not, and after eating, the form of the food — bread with its appearance intact, cooked dish, or fruit of the seven species — decides between three blessings, one abridged blessing, or none.

flowSteps.content: 📜 Rav & Shmuel: five grains → mezonot, even mixed; rice and millet excluded
❓ Rice bread 'like a cooked dish'? Rice listed among cooked dishes? Tosefta: cooked rice → mezonot — cannot be R' Yoḥanan ben Nuri, so it is the Rabbis → teyuvta
🍯 After the seven species: Rabban Gamliel three blessings, Sages me'ein shalosh; R' Akiva in Jericho follows the majority; Tosefta's rice clause emended to 'nothing'

columns.content: 🍞 Crumbs in a dish: Rav Yosef's olive-bulk → Rav Sheshet: hamotzi even smaller, if it looks like bread (Rava)
🥣 Rihata: both farmers' and Meḥoza's → mezonot; terokanin / terita / kutaḥ-bread and ḥalla

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Anything containing the five species of grain gets borei minei mezonot; bread keeps hamotzi as long as it retains the appearance of bread

quiz.q: Why did Rav and Shmuel need to state both 'anything that has of the five grains' and 'anything that is of the five grains'?
o: One refers to Eretz Yisrael, the other to Babylonia
One teaches that mixtures get mezonot; the other excludes rice and millet even in pure form
One refers to bread, the other to cooked dishes
One is Rav's view and the other is Shmuel's
quiz.e: 'Has of the five grains' teaches that even a mixture gets mezonot. 'Is of the five grains' teaches that rice and millet, which are not among the five, do not get mezonot even when eaten pure.

quiz.q: In what sense is rice bread 'like a cooked dish', according to the Gemara's first answer?
o: It receives mezonot before and me'ein shalosh after
It receives a blessing both before and after, though different ones: shehakol and borei nefashot
It may be used for matza on Passover
It is obligated in ḥalla
quiz.e: The Gemara distinguishes: like a cooked dish in requiring blessings before and after, but unlike it in which blessings — shehakol beforehand and borei nefashot afterward.

quiz.q: What does Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri hold about rice?
o: It is grain: one is liable to karet for its leaven and fulfills the matza obligation with it
It is a vegetable and receives borei peri ha'adama in every form
It is grain only when mixed with wheat
It never requires a blessing afterward
quiz.e: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says rice is a species of grain in every respect, so its leaven carries karet on Passover and matza baked from it fulfills the obligation. The Rabbis disagree.

quiz.q: How did Rabbi Akiva justify reciting the abridged blessing after dates despite Rabban Gamliel's view?
o: He claimed dates are not among the seven species
He said he had eaten less than an olive-bulk
He cited Rabban Gamliel's own teaching that in a dispute between an individual and the many, the halakha follows the many
He said the abridged blessing is permitted in Jericho
quiz.e: Rabbi Akiva told Rabban Gamliel: you taught us that when an individual disputes the many, the halakha follows the many, so he followed the Sages' ruling of one abridged blessing.

quiz.q: What is the final ruling about a cooked dish containing bread crumbs smaller than an olive-bulk?
o: Mezonot before and me'ein shalosh after, as Rav Yosef said
Hamotzi, provided the crumbs still have the appearance of bread
Shehakol, because the bread has lost its identity
Hamotzi only if the crumbs came from the meal-offerings
quiz.e: Rav Sheshet rules that one recites hamotzi even without olive-bulk pieces, and Rava qualifies that the crumbs must retain the appearance of bread (torita denahama).
